title: The Sparrow and the Peacock
logline: A careful little sparrow makes his friend the peacock king and becomes his minister; told to stay near a hunter's net because no one escapes fate, he avoids it faithfully until his duty as minister sends him down to stop a fight, and the net takes him.
moral: Neither rank nor caution can save you from what is fated; and the sense of duty that lifts you up can be the very thing that brings you down.
tone: Warm and lightly comic for the friendship and the election; quiet suspense once the net appears; a sober, gentle ending with no gloating and no violence shown.

beats.summary: The little sparrow visits the peacock every day, dawn to dusk.
He admires him: the fan opens and the sparrow is dazzled.
The birds meet on a mountain to choose a king; the throne is empty.
The crowned peacock makes the sparrow his minister (the badge).
One day the minister is late.
Flashback: the hunter's net snaps shut on two big birds beside the sparrow's nest.
The sparrow wants to move away.
The king forbids it: no one escapes his lot. The grand pose.
He stays and is careful: detours, lookouts, food far away.
Two sparrows fight on the open ground.
Duty beats caution: he must go down and make peace.
The net lands on all three.
Caught and handed to the companion; the cage shuts.
Neither office nor caution helped: the badge falls.
The former minister is carried away; the badge lies in the dust.

sets.description: Composed from Library pieces only, world 1000 x 1230, ground y 900: skyCycle (u animated 0.06 to 0.45), hillTrees, ground, one Library tree at the left edge with a low branch whose tip is the sparrow perch at about (330, 620) (measure on the set; add a branch stub if the tree has none there), two bushes at x 820 and x 120.

The planned 'rockyHill' set used at its top terrace only (window 1000 x 1230): grey rock terrace floor at y 900 across the width, a low ledge at the left (top y 810, x 40..300), a throne rock at x 720..900 with a flat top at y 790 and a tall back slab to y 600, a small stone post at x 540 (top y 800, 60 wide), far triangular peaks with snow caps at 40 % scale on the horizon, and a band of cloudFlat clouds BELOW the terrace edge (y 950..1150) to show height. Sky from skyCycle.

Composed from Library pieces, world 1600 x 1230, ground y 900: skyCycle + hillTrees + ground; the nest tree (Library tree(), trunk x 220, crowns above y 420) with the nest (nestDraw, no eggs) in a fork at about (300, 560) and a bare lookout branch whose tip is at about (430, 470); the net spot at x 760; a hiding bush at x 1060 (bush {w:270, h:150}); a far berry bush at x 1460 (bush with red dots); for S16 a far mountain silhouette on the horizon at x 1250 (the summit set as a flat shape 160 wide).

props.description: crownProp: three point gold crown 70 wide x 44 high with red dots on the points, black brush outline; ghost:true draws it as a dashed outline with a "?" inside. On the peacock it is the peacock field crown:1 (follows the head).

officeBadge: blue ribbon 10 wide across the chest from shoulder to hip with a gold medal r 9 (red centre dot) at the middle; as a loose prop it is a ribbon loop 50 long with the medal, with rot and a limp state for lying on the ground. On a bird: bird option badge:true.

The planned 'fishingNet' bigNet (diamond mesh, 22 unit cells, brown lines 3 wide, rope border with 6 small weights): states roll (bundle 60 x 40), spread (flat 280 x 14 on the ground with 4 pegs and a pull rope), bag (closed sack 150 x 170 with bulges), plus two states added here: thrown (disc opening 80 to 320 wide with rot) and draped (dome 320 x 130 over occupants, with tent:[x,y] pulling a cone up and bulge points).
grainPile: 30 to 40 yellow grains (ellipses 6 x 4, black outline 1.5) in a mound up to 70 wide x 22 high, fill 0..1; loose grains positioned by a seeded K.rng.
The planned 'birdCage' (KD-031): domed wire cage 170 x 200, hinged door (door 0..1.9 rad), carry ring, back and front bar passes so the sparrow sits inside.
The planned 'bindle' (KD-010): stick 60 long with a red dotted bundle r 16, carried over the sparrow shoulder or lying on the ground.
Library nest, no eggs or chicks (nestDraw with eggs 0), in the fork of the nest tree; rim drawn over the sparrow for the peek.
Library worm() and fig() (fig recoloured red as a berry) for the gifts to the king and the squabble prize.

subtitles.ar: كان عصفور صغير يزور طاووسًا كل صباح،|ويبقى معه حتى المساء. عرفه جيدًا وأعجب به.|وفي يوم اجتمعت الطيور فوق جبل|لتختار ملكًا يحل خلافاتها ويحفظ النظام بينها.
subtitles.en: A little sparrow visited a peacock|from morning until evening.|One day birds gathered on a mountain|to choose a king who would settle their disagreements.

subtitles.ar: اقترح العصفور أن يكون الطاووس ملكًا، فوافقت الطيور.|شكر الطاووس صديقه وجعله وزيرًا قريبًا منه.|صار العصفور يهتم بشؤون المملكة، ويأتي إلى الملك بالطعام والأخبار كل يوم.
subtitles.en: The sparrow proposed the peacock, and the birds agreed.|The new king made his friend a close minister,|who brought him food and news daily.

subtitles.ar: تأخر العصفور عن موعده يومًا، فسأله الطاووس عن السبب.|قال: «رأيت صيادًا ينصب شبكة قرب عشي، ويضع الحبوب داخلها.|وبعد قليل دخل طائران كبيران إلى الشبكة فأمسك بهما».
subtitles.en: One day the sparrow was late. Asked why,|he explained that a hunter had set a grain-baited net near his nest|and captured two large birds.

subtitles.ar: أخبر العصفور الملك أنه يريد ترك ذلك المكان خوفًا من الصياد.|لكن الطاووس قال له: «لا تغادر بيتك؛ فالإنسان لا يستطيع الهرب من نصيبه مهما احتاط».|أطاع العصفور الملك وبقي قرب عشه.
subtitles.en: The sparrow wanted to move away,|but the peacock advised him to stay, saying no one can escape fate.|The sparrow obeyed.

subtitles.ar: استمر العصفور في مراقبة المكان بحذر.|كان يتجنب الشبكة إذا رآها، ويبحث عن الطعام بعيدًا عنها.|ومع ذلك لم ينس ما حدث للطائرين اللذين أخذهما الصياد في ذلك اليوم.
subtitles.en: The sparrow remained watchful,|avoiding the net and finding food elsewhere.|He never forgot the birds taken by the hunter.

subtitles.ar: وفي يوم آخر رأى عصفورين يتشاجران على الأرض.|قال في نفسه: «كيف أكون وزيرًا للطيور وأتركهما يتقاتلان؟|يجب أن أنزل وأصلح بينهما قبل أن يؤذي أحدهما الآخر».
subtitles.en: Another day he saw two sparrows fighting on the ground.|As minister, he felt he should intervene|before they hurt each other.

subtitles.ar: نزل العصفور بسرعة بين المتشاجرين،|وفي تلك اللحظة ألقى الصياد شبكته على الثلاثة.|حاول الوزير أن يطير، لكنه وجد نفسه محاصرًا.|جاء الصياد وأمسكه، ثم سلمه إلى أحد رفاقه.
subtitles.en: He flew down between them,|and at that moment the hunter cast his net over all three.|The minister was trapped,|caught and handed to the hunter’s companion.

subtitles.ar: تذكر العصفور كلام الطاووس، وفكر في الخطر الذي كان يخشاه منذ البداية.|لم ينفعه منصبه ولا حذره هذه المرة.|ابتعد الصياد وهو يحمل الطائر الذي كان قبل قليل وزيرًا لملك الطيور.
subtitles.en: The sparrow recalled the peacock’s advice and the danger he had feared.|Neither his office nor his caution saved him|as the hunter carried off the former minister.

new_assets.name: peacock
new_assets.description: Side view peacock for this film and any later peacock, pheasant or proud bird tale. Feet at (x, y), facing dir. At s 1: about 330 tall to the crest tips; body a blue teardrop 130 wide x 170 tall with blue Ben-Day dots; neck an S curve 110 long, 34 wide; head r 34 with a white eye patch, yellow beak 30 long; crest of 5 thin stalks 40 long with dotted tips; legs 2 grey sticks 70 long. Train: fan 0 = folded bundle trailing 280 behind on the ground with 5 eye spots; fan 1 = half disc of radius 300 behind the body made of 13 feathers in two rows (green tapering stalks, each ending in an eye spot: yellow ring r 20, blue disc r 13, black centre r 6). Fields: fan 0..1, fanShake, neck (0.85..1.15), headRot, bow 0..1, talk/beak, brow, crest (-1..1), wing 0..1 (near wing raised as a hand; wingAng to aim it), sit 0..1 (train hangs down in front), crown 0..1, gulp 0..1 (bump travelling down the neck), ph/amp (walk), preen, plus the shared acting fields.
new_assets.implementation: One function in Library/cast (after approval). Body, neck and head as K paths with brush outlines; neck as a 3 point bezier whose control points come from neck/bow/headRot; fan feathers in a loop i = 0..12 at angle lerp(-80, 80 degrees) x fan, each delayed by |i-6| frames via the caller (stagger) or an internal open(i) = clamp(fan * 1.4 - |i-6| * 0.06); eye spots are three circles; shimmer = +-1.5 degrees sine per feather with phase i. Legs through walk(). Wrap with acting() in registry.js using the body blue as lid colour.

new_assets.name: sparrow (bird kind)
new_assets.description: A new kind 'sparrow' on the Library bird with three palettes: pal 0 hero (chestnut cap, grey cheek, black bib, cream belly, brown streaked wing), pal 1 paler with a grey cap, pal 2 redder with a larger bib. No crest. Option badge:true draws the officeBadge on the chest.
new_assets.implementation: Add a BIRD.sparrow palette entry (and pal variants) and a small bib/cap overlay in the bird function behind the kind test; every existing bird field (fly, flap, drop, headRot, sag, beak, lid, sq, tailDrop) works unchanged. Defaults of other kinds untouched (regression must stay identical).

new_assets.name: person costume presets (hunter)
new_assets.description: The planned 'hunter' (fowler) preset from KD-031: skull cap with a feather, stubble, sleeveless jerkin; a palette option gives the companion.
new_assets.implementation: One COSTUME table entry in cast/people.js (headwear cap + feather line with a 2 frame lag option, jerkin as robe with short length, stubble as beard dots); companion via pal overrides.

new_assets.name: rockyHill
new_assets.description: The planned bare mountain, used here only at its top terrace with a throne rock, a ledge, a stone post, far peaks and a cloud band below the edge (dimensions under sets.summit).
new_assets.implementation: Bake once: grey rock polygons with dot shading (S.halftone on the shadow side), far peaks as triangles at 40 % scale, cloudFlat row below y 950. Options throne:true, post:true so other stories can reuse the terrace.

new_assets.name: fishingNet
new_assets.description: The planned mesh drawing (KD-007, KD-031) with the bigNet states roll, spread and bag, extended with thrown (opening spinning disc) and draped (dome with tent point and bulges) for casting a net over birds.
new_assets.implementation: Mesh = two families of parallel lines clipped to the state outline (rectangle, ellipse, dome path, sack path). draped: outline is a dome path through tent/bulge points; draw a back pass before the occupants and a front pass after. thrown: ellipse scaled by open with rot. Rope as a quadratic curve that straightens with a taut 0..1 field.

new_assets.name: birdCage
new_assets.description: The planned domed wire cage 170 x 200 with a hinged door, carry ring and back/front bar passes (KD-031).
new_assets.implementation: As planned in KD-031; add a sway angle about the ring for swing().

new_assets.name: crownProp, officeBadge, grainPile
new_assets.description: Three small props: gold crown (solid or dashed ghost with "?"), minister badge (ribbon + medal, worn or loose), grain mound with fill 0..1 and loose grains.
new_assets.implementation: Flat shapes with brush outlines; the ghost crown uses a dashed stroke; grains from a seeded K.rng list computed once.

new_assets.name: bindle
new_assets.description: The planned bindle (from 'oilLamp, bindle, bigHand', KD-010), sized for a bird.
new_assets.implementation: A line and a dotted circle with a knot; swings a beat late with swing().

new_assets.name: fightCloud
new_assets.description: The planned comic scuffle cloud (KD-005, KD-016): churning dust puffs with stars, wings and feet poking out, hiding the fight.
new_assets.implementation: 8 to 10 dust puffs (circles) on seeded orbits around a centre, re-seeded every 3 frames; 3 stars; two wing shapes popping out at seeded angles.

new_assets.name: featherFall
new_assets.description: The planned feathers that rock down on seeded sway paths and rest on the ground; also one feather drifting up (S12).
new_assets.implementation: As planned (AN-036 and others): x = x0 + A sin(w t + ph), y eased down, rot = sway derivative.

new_assets.name: groundShadow
new_assets.description: The planned moving shadow on the ground, here with a mesh pattern for the shadow of the falling net (133.8 to 137.5).
new_assets.implementation: Flat ellipse at alpha 0.35 clipped to the ground band; option pattern:'mesh' strokes diagonal lines inside it.

new_assets.name: iconBalloon
new_assets.description: The planned wordless picture balloon, single mode, for the news whispered to the king (40.06).
new_assets.implementation: As planned: S.box style balloon with a tail and a small drawing inside.

new_assets.name: dream wash
new_assets.description: The planned blue halftone overlay and dotted vignette, used to mark the told flashback (S6).
new_assets.implementation: As planned (AN-095): panel-space halftone ring, alpha 0.25, drawn before finish.

owner_questions: The script names no crown or badge; I added a gold crown for the king and a blue ribbon with a medal as the minister's badge so "his office" can be seen and can fall off at 161.44 (default: keep both).
The sparrow is drawn as a new brown "sparrow" kind of the Library bird rather than reusing the lark as it is (default: new kind with three palettes).
The two "large birds" of the flashback are drawn as two Library crows at 1.25 scale (default: crows; doves or hawks would need another new drawing).

P7 says the bird is handed to a companion and P8 says the hunter carries him away; I put a cage in the companion's hands and have the hunter take the cage back at 164.68 (default: cage, hunter carries it).

The hunter is hinted behind the bush from 113.3 (a feather, then eyes at 120.75) before the narration mentions him, for suspense; the fight itself is staged as genuine, not as bait (default: keep the hint, no bait).
The final image adds the peacock as a tiny distant silhouette waiting beside an empty place, which the script does not say (default: keep; it can be replaced by a hold on the fallen badge).
Capture is shown without harm: a hand closes round the bird, a cage door shuts, and the two other sparrows leave as shapes in a net sack (default: as described).

English comic lettering used: MORNING, EVENING, WOW!, SQUAWK!, YES!, MINISTER, KINGDOM, DAY 1 2 3, LATE!, NET, MY NEST, GRAIN, SNAP!, I MUST GO!, STAY!, FATE, HOME, FAR AWAY, POW!, ON THE GROUND, MINISTER!, STOP!, 1 2 3, TRAPPED!, CLANK! (default: all kept; cut to about 14 if the film reads cluttered).
implementation_notes: Start from Library/template. Three baked sets (garden, summit, glade); glade is 1600 wide so clamp the camera with WW = 1600 there. Use panel-only shake as in the template.
Set LIFE.t = t each frame so every bird and person blinks; give explicit lids hand blinks. Each bird in the flock needs its own seed.

All cue times are word starts from timeline.md; a word start may include up to 0.4 s of silence, so check the snap (63.06), the crown (27.3), the net landing (137.56) and the door (149.9) against the audio envelope and shift by a few frames if needed.

The narration is almost continuous: the only pause of 0.6 s or more is 20.90-22.12. Sound effects are therefore limited to 5.0, 7.9, 21.3, 86.9, 120.8 and 172.75. The net throw, the snap and the cage door are silent visual hits (lettering only) unless the animator finds real micro gaps in the envelope.
Peacock FATE_POSE (80.22) must be one constant object reused inside the thought cloud at 153.34 so setup and payoff match exactly.

Inside thought clouds reuse the scene draw functions with a remapped clock (S10 replays S6 60.9-63.4 in 1.6 s); keep figures at least about 110 px on screen (cloud scale 0.3 to 0.4, birds drawn at double size inside if needed).
Hiding: draw the hunter first and the bush over him (no clipped second copy). In S11-S12 only the feather and later the eyes show. Mesh of the draped net: back pass, birds, front pass.

The hand closing on the bird: draw palm, then the bird (sq 0.85), then four finger ellipses over it; use handRW world targets so the arm IK follows the lift (arms are about 74 units long, so the hunter must stand within reach: bend with lean 0.25 and kneel 0.5).
Sizes: sparrow s 0.8 (about 90 px tall), peacock s 1.0 (330 tall), people s 1.0 (240 tall). In two-shots with a person and the sparrow use zoom 2.2 or more on the hand and bird.
The person figure is front facing; the throw reads through arm angles (raised [2.45, 2.85] to forward) and body tip, not a profile.
One LATER card only, at 107.18 with the caption ANOTHER DAY...; hide the dawn sky change and the removal of the old net under its covered midpoint.
Subtitle chunks are in "subtitles" (verbatim, split by word counts from script.json). No en or em dashes anywhere on screen.
After moving peacock, sparrow kind, hunter preset, fishingNet, birdCage and the small props into Library/, run node Library/tests/regression.mjs (must say all identical) and rebuild the catalogue.
warnings: New drawing load is above the usual four: peacock (L), rockyHill terrace (M), fishingNet with two extra states (M) and several small props and effects (S). Most are already planned by other stories (hunter, fishingNet, birdCage, rockyHill, fightCloud, featherFall, groundShadow, iconBalloon, dream wash, bindle); only peacock, the sparrow kind and three small props are new names.
The English subtitle is a summary and shorter than the Arabic; chunk boundaries therefore do not line up word for word (for example P4 chunk 2).
The first word of P3 (42.00, 2.0 s long) and of several paragraphs carries leading silence; S5 uses that silence for the waiting king. Do not place sound there without measuring the envelope.
S9 covers the end of P4 (84.56-86.62) and P5 to 99.2 on purpose: "he stayed near his nest" plays on the nest.
